correctness.rationale: PASS: reconstructed F=B^T B for GF(2) unoriented cube incidence and L=BB^T, then identified L as multiplication by s=sum_i y_i in the square-zero group algebra. s²=0 implies F³=0. For augmentation ideal I, ker B^T=<product_i y_i>, dim sI=2^{d-1}-1 and this all-ones vector lies in sI for d>=2; hence ranks N-2 and N/2-2. Rank differences give #Jordan-3=N/2-2, #Jordan-2=2, #Jordan-1=(d-3)N/2+2 and exact nullities. Separate direct-adjacency GF(2) computation agrees for dimensions d=2..6. The d=1 exception is explicitly excluded. Finite cases are corroboration, the square-zero algebra is the universal proof.
